message_source_quote: the decisive paper was `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md`, which documents the exact mechanism for this task: a *stance* vector injected at mid-depth (layers 20–24) with a large dose, making the layers above the band keep developing the implied concept instead of dropping it for next-token prediction.
writeup_source_quote: The vector is directionally related to the white-bear "think/don't think" stance (cosine near 0.8) but is a distinct, task-aligned contrast: an inference-on / inference-off stance, not the maintenance or suppression of a named concept.

claims_about_writeup.quote: `submission/contribution.md` — 213 words describing the stance vector, its construction from self-authored held-out pairs, and the result.
claims_about_writeup.why: The contribution.md text is approximately 213-214 words and does describe the stance vector's construction from the 30 self-authored pairs used on the fit split (effectively held out from the benchmark item set) and the resulting pass@10 figure, matching the message's description.

differences.what: Naming the source and framing it as 'the decisive paper' whose mechanism the method directly follows
differences.message_quote: the decisive paper was `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md`, which documents the exact mechanism for this task
differences.writeup_quote: The vector is directionally related to the white-bear "think/don't think" stance (cosine near 0.8) but is a distinct, task-aligned contrast

differences.what: Explicit reproduction/validation of the source method with matched published values and its own measured performance (pass@10 0.69), as a step before building the new vector
differences.message_quote: Validated the mechanism end-to-end by rebuilding the white-bear direction from `directed_modulation` items — my captured per-layer gap norms matched the paper's published values (4.62/4.86/4.91/5.39/5.80), and steering at k=6 reached pass@10 0.69 on this split.
differences.writeup_quote: It was not built from any benchmark item set.

differences.what: Comparative framing of the new method's performance against the reproduced source method ('on par with')
differences.message_quote: It peaks at k=11, reaching **strict pass@10 = 0.706**, on par with the think/don't-think direction but as a distinct inference-on/inference-off contrast.
differences.writeup_quote: On association's fit split it reaches strict pass@10 of 0.71 against a baseline of 0.13.

rationale: The message explicitly names and files the source as papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md, calls it the decisive paper whose mechanism it reproduced and validated numerically (matching published per-layer norms, pass@10 0.69) before building a 'genuinely different' stance vector that it says performs 'on par with' the reproduced source. The write-up, by contrast, only mentions 'white-bear' informally as a directionally related (cosine ~0.8) but distinct stance, never names the paper file, never reports a reproduction step or its score, and stresses the vector was not built from any benchmark item set — so the message credits and quantifies the source relationship far more explicitly than the write-up does, while both agree the final method is a distinct, task-aligned contrast rather than the source's maintenance/suppression stance.
